title: Injecting Distributional Awareness into MLLMs via Reinforcement Learning for Deep Imbalanced Regression
claim: Standard fine-tuning collapses predictions onto a few high-density values under skewed training data; ours spreads predictions across the whole range.
layout: 3 vertically stacked histograms sharing x-axis; middle panel overlays two methods
description: Three vertically stacked histograms share one x-axis running from 0 to 100. The top panel, 'Imbalanced train label density', shows blue bars and a smoothed curve. The curve is a skewed bell peaking around 35 and with thin tails. The bottom panel, 'Nearly balanced test label density', is a flat plateau of blue bars at about 30 samples per bin from roughly 18 to 78, tapering at both ends. The middle panel, 'Test prediction frequency', is the focus. Tall orange spikes for SFT sit at a few discrete values such as 25, 35, 65 and 75, and reach about 220 counts. Shorter, more evenly spread blue bars for the proposed method fill the gaps and cover the tails. The eye goes first to the orange spikes.
caption: SFT exhibits a pronounced regression-to-the-mean effect, with predictions collapsing toward the many-shot region. Our method produces a substantially more balanced prediction distribution and maintains reliable predictions in tail regions.
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) struggle with numerical regression under long-tailed target distributions. Token-level supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and point-wise regression rewards bias learning toward high-density regions, leading to regression-to-the-mean behavior and poor tail performance. We identify the lack of cross-sample relational supervision as a key limitation of existing MLLM training paradigms. To address it, we propose a distribution-aware reinforcement learning framework based on Group Relative Policy Optimization, which introduces batch-level comparison-based supervision via the Concordance Correlation Coefficient-based reward to align predicted and ground-truth distributions in terms of correlation, scale, and mean. The framework is plug-and-play, requiring no architectural modification. Experiments on a unified suite of long-tailed regression benchmarks show consistent improvements over SFT and existing MLLM regression methods, with particularly strong gains in medium- and few-shot regimes.
